observabilityFinding.claim: Pine `table` objects are readable from the DOM
observabilityFinding.evidence: The chart carried 3 DOM <table> elements and 32 canvases, and a full-document text scan found ZERO occurrences of the status-table headers ('Frame', 'Freshness', 'Trend', 'Session', 'Bias'). Pine tables render on canvas.
observabilityFinding.workingChannel: The Data Window. TradingView tags each row with its own test hook `data-test-id-value-title`, so label/value pairs are readable without depending on hashed class names. Verified: 23 rows read, all Session Context diagnostics present.
observabilityFinding.consequenceForR4: A `table.new` readback fixture would NOT be DOM-readable either. The R4 comparison gate therefore needs the CTX channels exposed through the Data Window (i.e. not display.none), not an on-chart table.
